Lunar Lander — launch splash
The game’s own title screen, held under its prompt, at 80 × 24.
The game

A small spacecraft. An unforgiving Moon.

Guide a fragile lander between lunar ridges and onto an illuminated pad. Every correction costs fuel. Read your drift, manage the descent and put both feet down safely, in a landscape drawn entirely in ANSI colour, with a distant Earth hanging over the ranges.

Fly the descent

Control tilt and throttle through deterministic lunar physics. Burn early to slow the fall, cancel sideways drift and straighten up above the lit pad.

Work through the chapters

Start in the training basin, then fly fifteen ranked missions in three chapters, Maria, Highlands and Frontier, from calm mare plains to narrow polar footholds. A daily challenge gives every pilot on the node the same flight and changes at the node’s local midnight.

Earn your wings

Every safe landing earns a gold, silver or bronze medal, and your career climbs from Cadet to Lunar Ace. Best landings go on each mission’s leaderboard, and with game events on, the node announces promotions and first golds.

At the keyboard

Inside Lunar Lander

Every frame below is drawn by Lunar Lander v0.1.0, the release NetBBS bundles, flying its own physics. An autopilot pressed the keys; nothing was drawn or edited by hand.

Lunar Lander — flight director
Pick a chapter and a mission. The briefing shows the pad, the fuel and your medals so far.

Play on NetBBS

Open Doors on a NetBBS node that offers Lunar Lander and choose the game. You need a terminal of at least 80 × 24; the flight pauses below that until you enlarge the window. Your best landing on each mission is kept, and every node has its own leaderboards.

A little thrust goes a long way.

Choose a mission, then press Enter. W/S or the up/down arrows adjust throttle; A/D or left/right tilt the craft. Controls stay set, so you do not need to hold two keys. Space cuts thrust, X levels the lander, P pauses and ? opens the flight manual.

At touchdown, both feet must be inside the pad, vertical speed no more than 3 m/s, sideways drift no more than 2 m/s and tilt within 10 degrees of upright. The numeric readings and pad lights are your precise references; the lander is drawn larger to keep it visible.

For SysOps

Lunar Lander is bundled with NetBBS from 7.41.0. Register it from Content ▸ Doors ▸ Gallery. Pilot records live beside the node database and are included in node backups. The door setup guide has the details, and the game’s repository has its releases and its own guide. Standalone, python lunar_lander.py runs it in any ANSI terminal for unranked practice.
